title: Officials Say Captain and Passengers Stopped Co-Pilot's Attempt to Crash FlyDubai Plane
summary:
A FlyDubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv faced a serious emergency on Wednesday. The plane landed safely in Saudi Arabia, and the passengers later reached Israel on a replacement aircraft.

Israeli officials said a co-pilot tried to crash the plane after he stabbed the captain. Flightradar24, a flight-tracking website, said the aircraft's data appeared to show that it descended suddenly and rapidly by nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds. The plane then sent a general emergency signal and, several minutes later, another signal that indicated possible unlawful interference. It diverted over Jordanian airspace toward Saudi Arabia. The airport in Tabuk said the flight made a distress call at 8:44 a.m. local time and landed safely at 9:45 a.m.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu identified the captain as Smit Machchhar, an Indian citizen, and noted his "extraordinary bravery." The Indian Embassy in Saudi Arabia said Machchhar was in stable condition in a hospital. Netanyahu said on X that the captain fought back, opened the cockpit door and enabled passengers and crew to overpower the attacker. "He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals," Netanyahu said. Israel's Foreign Ministry said the people on board were from Israel, India and the U.A.E., and the U.S. State Department said four passengers had American citizenship.

Passengers told CBC News that they were shocked by the sudden drop and did not know what was happening. Adam Polo said they later realized the pilot had gotten the cockpit door open, the alleged attacker was subdued and another pilot got control of the aircraft. After arriving in Israel, passenger Lital Shachaf said, "it was a miracle."

The passengers reached Ben Gurion International Airport in Tel Aviv on Wednesday evening, more than 10 hours later. Netanyahu said the co-pilot was being questioned by Saudi authorities, though it was not clear whether that was taking place in the hospital. Israeli officials said the motive remained under investigation, and Saudi authorities said an investigation was underway.

FlyDubai said its flights to and from Israel would be suspended while an investigation takes place. The route has become popular among Israelis since Israel and the U.A.E., which includes Dubai, normalized relations in 2020.
why_it_matters: The story shows how an emergency in the air can involve people from several countries and why investigators and governments take time to find the facts.
